summary.headline: CAMS Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 10% YoY to INR415 crore, with EBITDA up 13.5% to INR191 crore and margin at 46%.
summary.overview: Operating revenue crossed INR400 crore for the first time, up 10% YoY, while EBITDA grew 13.5% to about INR191 crore after absorbing deferred employee increments from Q1. EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 46% and PAT rose 14.5% YoY. MF AUM grew about 12.5% to INR58.5 lakh crore (67% share), with equity AUM up 15.5% versus industry 15.2%. Non-MF revenue grew about 21-22% YoY to just under 16% of revenue, led by CAMSPay (up over 50% YoY) and KRA's recovery.

financial_highlights.change: +150 bps YoY; +11% QoQ growth in non-MF revenue
After ~INR160 crore dividends paid in quarter
Includes INR8.5 crore annual appraisal impact (~2%)

segments.name: Mutual fund (asset-based)
segments.commentary: CAMS MF AUM about INR58.5 lakh crore, up ~12.5%, 67% market share; equity AUM up 15.5% vs industry 15.2%, with ~70% share of industry equity net sales over last year. Gross SIP collections up 16.5% vs industry 12.4%.

segments.name: CAMSPay (payments)
segments.commentary: Revenue up over 50% YoY and 13% QoQ; now over 6% of revenue (vs ~3% two to two-and-a-half years ago). Base now about INR100 crore-plus; management guides ~30% growth p.a. for next two years.

segments.name: KRA (KYC registration)
segments.commentary: Revenue rebounded QoQ despite price cut from April; share of demat/broking segment rising; 5 of top 10 broking houses are clients. Incremental revenue from Phase 1 status-inquiry APIs estimated at ~INR1.5 crore.

segments.name: Alternatives / AIF
segments.commentary: Revenue up 22% YoY; AUM just crossed INR3.3 lakh crore; 50-plus new mandates and 15 new marquee relationships. Management describes AIF as services-heavy with ~20% margin.

segments.name: Repository (demat and insurance)
segments.commentary: Crossed 15 million (1.5 crore) demat accounts; Bima Central broker module launched. Account aggregator revenue up 19% on a small base.

guidance_outlook: Yield: FY27 decline guided at ~3% YoY (less than 2.5% in a good quarter, ~3% in a reasonable quarter); QoQ decline was under 1%. Management sees no revision needed.
Non-MF: target ~20% growth and ~20% profitability exit; target non-MF share of sales to reach 20% within a couple of years. Non-MF margin steady-state of 25%+ seen in 3 years.

Expenses: management aims to keep expense growth below 10%; Q3 and Q4 platform costs expected to rise from ~INR5 crore to ~INR8 crore then ~INR9.5-10 crore per quarter, net incremental opex only ~INR1.5-2 crore per quarter after offsets.
CAMSPay growth: expect around early 30% per year over next two years rather than 50%.
Margins: normal years expected to expand 100-200 bps; new platform headcount trend (~250-300 fewer) expected to continue for at least 3 more years.
UPI MDR: limited upside, ~INR1-2 crore per year on a ~INR100 crore payments base.
Large AMC renewals: management says yield discounts will not be disproportionate; next year's renewals with a couple of large customers flagged.
capex_capacity: Re-architecture (FUNDSNet) platform about 30% complete; FUNDSNet live and legacy utility to be sunset by March/April 2027.
Cumulative platform cost taken to opex about INR27 crore to date; Q2 platform cost ~INR5 crore (INR2.5 crore opex plus INR1.5 crore depreciation, per CFO).
Depreciation rose INR3.5 crore QoQ to ~INR28 crore; more than INR1.5 crore attributed to new modules going live; storage server capitalisation also raised it.
Headcount about 8,200, down from ~8,450 at start of year (250-300 reduction through non-backfilling).
Several hundred crore of SEBI-mandated investment cited as a cost driver in yield negotiations.
GIFT City retail funds: AUM above INR1,500 crore after 5 launches, with 2-3 more expected in Q3. SIF AUM about INR20,000 crore across ~12 AMCs.
demand_pricing: Equity net sales share ~70% of industry over last year; gross SIP collections +16.5% YoY vs industry 12.4%.

Yield drop ~3% YoY attributed to scale-based telescopic pricing (~2% in a normal year), mix shift from debt to passives (debt yield ~2-2.25 bps replaced by passives ~0.5 bps), and customer mix; management denies large discounts or renewal discounts.
Client base: 32 of 64 licensed AMCs; InCred AMC appointed CAMS as RTA; ASK Investments and Carnelian went live; Oaklane and Neo expected in Q3.
Non-MF asset-linked vs transaction revenue: non-asset-based MF revenue (transactions, MFCentral, call centre, NFO) is not asset-linked; NFOs fell sharply YoY.
Competition: management says the industry faces pressure from AI-enabled in-sourcing and AMC price negotiations, but argues outsourcing persists at scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will CAMSPay growth moderate given the high base, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects around early 30% growth per year over the next two years rather than 50%, with 50% possibly lasting one or two more quarters; growth driven by cards business added on top of payment aggregator licence.

qa_highlights.question: How much of KRA's rebound is volume versus repricing, and is ~INR100 crore a quarter a fair run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it mainly to usage growth and new clients in demat/broking, with the Phase 1 API contributing only about INR1.5 crore incremental revenue; expects growth to continue over time, with no run-rate figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 employee cost a fair run-rate going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Q2 employee cost can be taken as run-rate, with no one-offs in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Could new AMCs or large-AMC renegotiations drag yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Newer AMCs (last 5 years) are estimated at 5-7% of AUM and revenue; management says better pricing on those young AMCs offsets; renewal discussions for large customers in FY28 will not be commented on yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new platform's P&L drag and trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Platform costs to rise from ~INR5 crore to ~INR8 crore, then ~INR9.5-10 crore per quarter over the next two quarters, but net incremental drag only ~INR1.5-2 crore per quarter after productivity offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Will UPI MDR benefit CAMSPay materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Very little: MDR of ~40 bps on UPI financial transactions versus ~2 bps on MF transactions, implying only ~INR1-2 crore a year benefit on a ~INR100 crore book.

risks_watch: Yield pressure: FY27 guided ~3% decline; renewal of a couple of large AMC contracts in FY28 is an open question and management declined to comment on terms.
AI and digital disruption of RTA/outsourcing models; management says in-sourcing is still distant but flagged possible digital regulation impact in next 2-3 quarters.
Platform cost ramp: Q3 and Q4 platform costs expected to rise to INR8-10 crore per quarter before offset by productivity; headcount reduction must sustain.
AUM growth moderation: management acknowledges that MF AUM growth of 7-8% would require a different response; cost control depends on productivity.
CAMSPay growth normalising from 50% toward ~30%; KRA revenue sensitive to capital market activity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on earnings quality and cost control, with emphasis that Q2 was not one-off; cautious and evasive on FY28 large-AMC renewals and on the AI/digital disruption question, which management answered only in general terms.
key_quotes: This is the first time we have crossed the INR400 crores mark.
The good news is that this is not a cash-guzzling business.
We will continue to remain a sold product, a significantly sold product, not a sought product.
So overall, this business, the non-MF business, grew almost 22%.

adds.what: FUNDSNet re-architecture platform (about 30% complete; live and legacy utility sunset by March/April 2027)
Bima Central broker module (launched); new modules going live

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 yield decline of ~3%, non-MF growth ~20% with ~20% profitability exit, CAMSPay ~30% growth for two years, and expense growth below 10%; backing is partly specific (MF AUM +12.5%, CAMSPay +50%, 15 new AIF relationships, onboarding of named AMCs) but no revenue growth number is given and the FUNDSNet platform is only ~30% complete.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 100-200 bps margin expansion in normal years and EBITDA margin already rose 140 bps YoY to 46%, but Q3-Q4 platform costs rise to ~INR9.5-10 crore per quarter, with net drag of only ~INR1.5-2 crore per quarter after offsets.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; the only build is the FUNDSNet software re-architecture (~30% complete, sunset by March/April 2027), which is a platform, not physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: MF AUM up ~12.5% to INR58.5 lakh crore, equity AUM +15.5% vs industry 15.2%, gross SIP collections +16.5% vs industry 12.4%, and CAMSPay guided at ~30% growth p.a. for two years, though yield falls ~3% in FY27 and AUM growth of 7-8% would need a different response.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Depreciation rose to ~INR28 crore and the platform is being built internally; no utilisation level was given and no new capex programme was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held guidance (yield decline ~3%, expense growth below 10%, non-MF ~20% growth) and sees no revision needed, with no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Yield drop of ~3% in FY27 with a large AMC renewal open for FY28, digital regulation flagged for the next 2-3 quarters, and CAMSPay normalising from 50% toward ~30%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Oaklane and Neo onboarding expected in Q3, 2-3 more GIFT City retail fund launches expected in Q3, and CAMSPay card business is scaling on top of the payment aggregator licence.

rows.label: Non-MF revenue scaling toward 20% of sales
rows.why: Non-MF revenue grew ~21-22% YoY to just under 16% of revenue, with non-MF profitability near 19% vs under 15% last quarter and a ~20% FY27 exit target.

rows.label: AIF and GIFT City expansion
rows.why: AIF AUM crossed INR3.3 lakh crore with 50-plus new mandates and 15 new marquee relationships, and GIFT City retail AUM is above INR1,500 crore with 2-3 more launches in Q3.

rows.label: Headcount reduction via non-backfilling
rows.why: Headcount fell from ~8,450 to ~8,200 (250-300 fewer) and management expects the trend to continue for at least 3 more years.

tone.note: Management was confident on earnings quality, cost control and the ~3% yield guide, and cautious or evasive on FY28 large-AMC renewals and AI/digital disruption; analysts pressed on CAMSPay normalisation, yield pressure and the platform cost ramp.
